question: How is plasma held without touching any wall?
answer: Plasma at millions of degrees would wreck any material it touched, so nothing solid holds it. Instead, a complex system of magnetic fields keeps it isolated from the walls and under control.
move: In a fusion reactor, the real wall is made of magnetic fields.

web.label: A ring-shaped reactor view with a button to release hot plasma into the ring and a switch to turn on the magnets. It asks how plasma is held without touching any wall, and invites you to watch the wall as the plasma is released.
